gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 identifies the same block-affine construction defect: Delta_j has no specified uniform distribution, so the admissible zero shift makes the zero output deterministic and invalidates one-fold and hence two-fold uniformity. Its repair explicitly supplies independent uniform entries for every Delta_j.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The block-affine scramble claims uniformity without imposing the required iid-uniform law on the translation vectors Delta_j; a degenerate shift therefore prevents the asserted one-fold and two-fold uniformity.

component_coverage.gold_component: The block-affine construction omits the distributional premise for Delta_j, permitting Delta_j=0 and thereby failing one-fold and two-fold uniformity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly states the missing Delta_j distribution, gives the zero-shift counterexample, derives failure of one-fold and two-fold uniformity, and supplies the iid-uniform repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-009 identifies the same gain-normalization defect: the defined double sum has an extra factor 1/n, making G=S/(n^2D) while the variance theorem and gain identities require S/(nD). It gives a concrete variance contradiction and a repair restoring the correct normalization and downstream factors.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The gain coefficient is mis-normalized by an extra factor 1/n, causing incompatibility between the definition, variance formula, exact gain identities, and downstream variance calculations.

component_coverage.gold_component: The definition of G uses S/[n^2 product_j(b_j-1)] instead of S/[n product_j(b_j-1)], producing incompatible variance and gain identities and requiring corresponding downstream factor corrections.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly derives the incorrect S/(n^2D) normalization, contrasts it with the required S/(nD), demonstrates the resulting variance mismatch, and specifies normalization and downstream corrections.
